subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What Telegram behavior should OpenClaw own when a voice message is discovered late or an already-dispatched voice turn aborts before any visible direct-chat reply?
rationale: Current source can support several plausible fixes, but choosing a latency threshold, restart/alert policy, and direct-chat fallback text changes user-visible Telegram behavior and needs owner intent before automation should implement it.

options.title: Define contract before implementation
options.body: Keep this open for maintainer review, require live/replayed Telegram proof, then implement the agreed latency watchdog and fallback semantics in one focused change.

options.title: Split the remaining work
options.body: Track ingress latency and aborted/no-visible-reply delivery as separate canonical issues if maintainers decide they need different owners or proof paths.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics first
options.body: Add source-age logging without automatic restart or visible fallback, accepting that the user-visible failure remains until a later product decision.

recommendation.title: Define contract before implementation
recommendation.body: Keep this open for maintainer review, require live/replayed Telegram proof, then implement the agreed latency watchdog and fallback semantics in one focused change.

likelyOwner.reason: The polling liveness history is the closest owner signal for the source-age/dispatch-latency part of the decision.
